subject.title: feat: add live-validated Zoom meeting guest plugin

question: Should Zoom guest transport ship as a bundled OpenClaw plugin with automatic browser media permissions and paired-node audio-command support, or should it remain an externally distributed plugin until that ownership boundary is explicitly approved?
rationale: Existing meeting plugins provide a relevant pattern, but this PR introduces a new bundled service integration, command-configured audio routing, browser permission grants, and a new startup plugin; protected maintainer handling requires an explicit product and trust-boundary decision.

options.title: Sponsor bundled Zoom support
options.body: Approve the bundled plugin direction after the two functional blockers and real-session evidence are resolved, with the plugin retaining Zoom-specific policy and lifecycle behavior.

options.title: Route it externally first
options.body: Keep the generic meeting seams and publish the Zoom integration as an external plugin until bundled distribution and permission ownership are separately approved.

options.title: Narrow the scope
options.body: Accept a transcribe-only or no-node-command variant if maintainers want to avoid the talk-back and paired-node trust surface in this release.

recommendation.title: Sponsor bundled Zoom support
recommendation.body: Approve the bundled plugin direction after the two functional blockers and real-session evidence are resolved, with the plugin retaining Zoom-specific policy and lifecycle behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The available evidence connects this person to the implementation and to the dependency/security review context; independent feature-history attribution could not be completed after the read-only sandbox failure.
